what_its_for: Tapentadol is a strong prescription pain medicine (opioid) used to treat moderate to severe pain in adults. The extended-release (ER) form is used for around-the-clock pain that requires long-term treatment, such as pain from diabetic nerve damage.
how_to_take: Take tapentadol exactly as your doctor prescribes. Swallow tablets whole with a full glass of water — do not crush, chew, or break them, especially the extended-release tablets, as this can release too much medicine at once and cause serious harm or death. You may take it with or without food. Do not take more doses or take it more often than directed.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on the lowest dose that controls your pain and may adjust it over time. Immediate-release tablets are usually taken every 4 to 6 hours as needed. Extended-release tablets are usually taken every 12 hours (twice a day). Never change your dose on your own. If you feel the medicine is not working, talk to your doctor before making any changes.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — UNLESS it is almost time for your next dose. If it is nearly time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store tapentadol at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep all tablets in a safe, secure place — preferably locked — out of reach of children, family members, and visitors. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet unless the label says it is safe to do so. Use a medicine take-back program to dispose of leftover pills safely.
what_to_avoid: Do NOT drink alcohol while taking tapentadol — combining them can cause dangerous breathing problems and may be fatal. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing anything that requires sharp focus until you know how this medicine affects you, as it can cause dizziness and drowsiness. Do not take other opioids, sleeping pills, muscle relaxers, anti-anxiety medicines, or antidepressants without first telling your doctor, as these combinations can be very dangerous. Do not stop taking tapentadol suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can cause withdrawal symptoms.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: slow, shallow, or stopped breathing; extreme drowsiness or difficulty waking up; confusion or unusual behavior; seizures; severe dizziness or fainting; a fast or irregular heartbeat; signs of a severe allergic reaction such as hives, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing; or signs of adrenal problems such as nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, or unusual tiredness. Also call your doctor if you feel the medicine is not controlling your pain or if you feel dependent on it.
when_it_works: The immediate-release form usually starts working within 30 to 60 minutes after you take it. The extended-release form builds up slowly over time and may take a day or two to reach a steady, consistent level of pain relief in your body.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: Tapentadol can harm an unborn baby and cause serious withdrawal symptoms in a newborn. Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. BREASTFEEDING: This medicine passes into breast milk and can harm a nursing baby. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. ELDERLY (65 and older): Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects like drowsiness, dizziness, and breathing problems. Your doctor may start you on a lower dose. CHILDREN: Tapentadol is not approved for use in patients under 18 years of age. KIDNEY OR LIVER PROBLEMS: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted or this medicine may not be safe for you.
